intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Washington County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: The results of our tests disclosed no instances of noncompliance or other matters that are required to be reported under Government Auditing Standards.
verdicts.detail: On internal control, the auditors wrote: “During our audit we did not identify any deficiencies in internal control that we consider to be material weaknesses.”

limits: From the 2023 report, dated November 17, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.name: Tontitown
cities.quote: Mayor On August 4, 2022, the City entered into a contract with a vendor for IT support/services. In addition to monthly payments to the vendor between September 2024 and January 2025, the City paid $27,840 to an individual who was apparently employed by the vendor for equivalent IT support/services. The City also paid the individual $15,684 in advance for equipment the City did not receive. On March 14, 2025, the City invoiced the individual for a portion of the undelivered equipment; as of report date, the City had not received the equipment or been reimbursed.
